## Calculated Values {#sec-calculated}

Parameters derived from mathematical formulas and economic models.

### Ratio of Military to Government Clinical Trials Spending: 604:1 {#sec-military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Ratio of global military spending to government clinical trials spending

**Inputs**:

- [Global Military Spending in 2024](#sec-global_military_spending_annual_2024) 📊: $2.72 trillion
- [Annual Global Government Spending on Clinical Trials](#sec-global_government_clinical_trials_spending_annual) 📊: $4.5 billion (95% CI: $3 billion - $6 billion)

$$
\begin{gathered}
Ratio_{mil:gov} \\
= \frac{Spending_{mil}}{Spending_{trials,gov}} \\
= \frac{\$2.72T}{\$4.5B} \\
= 604
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

## External Data Sources {#sec-external}

Parameters sourced from peer-reviewed publications, institutional databases, and authoritative reports.

### Annual Global Government Spending on Clinical Trials: $4.5 billion {#sec-global_government_clinical_trials_spending_annual}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Annual global government spending on interventional clinical trials (~5-10% of total)

**Source**: [@global-government-clinical-trial-spending-estimate]

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: 95% CI: [$3 billion, $6 billion] • Distribution: Lognormal (SE: $1 billion)

**What this means**: There's significant uncertainty here. The true value likely falls between $3 billion and $6 billion (±33%). This represents a wide range that our Monte Carlo simulations account for when calculating overall uncertainty in the results.

*The lognormal distribution means values can't go negative and have a longer tail toward higher values (common for costs and populations).*
